resolutions.recommendation: add Mississippi to StartState/Province (or otherwise record the true multi-state origin) — the sheet's 'Mobile County, Alabama' start point is where the line is compressed, not where it originates
resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet's Location [ref] unit has StartLocation='Mobile County', StartState/Province='Alabama' only (EndState/Province='Florida' is fine). THREE independent sources disagree with treating Alabama as the sole/primary origin: (1) Wikipedia's article states the line 'brings gas from Mississippi and Alabama...to Florida' — Mississippi named first; (2) hydrocarbons-technology.com states 'The pipeline originates from a gas gathering system in Mississippi and terminates in Coden, a coastal fishing village in southern Mobile County, Alabama. Here, the gas is compressed at compressor station (CS) 410' — i.e. Mobile County AL is a compression/receipt point mid-route, not the true upstream origin, which is a Mississippi gas-gathering system; (3) FERC's 2019-06-21 Federal Register notice for the Phase VI expansion independently states the added capacity runs 'from existing points of receipt in Mississippi and Alabama to an existing point of delivery in Manatee County, Florida' — a regulator document, naming both states as receipt points. gem.wiki itself (read for leads only, not cited) also says 'runs from Mississippi and Alabama.' All of this matches the scope note's flagged route-vs-sheet disagreement for this row. The EndLocation cell is also blank; independent sources place the Gulf landfall at Port Manatee/Manatee County, FL, with the line continuing onshore through Polk and Martin counties to a terminus in Pinellas County (hydrocarbons-technology.com) — a more precise EndLocation than the sheet currently records. Recommend Update route the StartState/Province fix (add Mississippi) and consider a more specific EndLocation (Manatee County / Pinellas County, FL) sourced the same way.

resolutions.recommendation: update Capacity — sheet's 1310.00 MMcf/d looks like a pre-Phase-VI figure; current operator-stated capacity is 1,378 MMcf/d (1.378 Bcf/d)
resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet records Capacity=1310.00 MMcf/d (LastUpdated 2022-10-11). gem.wiki attributes 1.31 Bcf/d to its 'Wikipedia' citation, but the actual Wikipedia article (verified live, read in full) is a two-sentence stub that states no capacity figure at all — that lineage does not hold up. Independent sources instead show: hydrocarbons-technology.com (2012 vintage, i.e. pre-Phase-VI) states 1.29 Bcf/d = 1290 MMcf/d; the operator's own CURRENT Fast Facts page (gulfstreamgas.com, live 2026) states 'Capacity: 1.378 billion cubic feet per day' = 1378 MMcf/d, and explicitly logs 'Phase VI in-service July 2022' as the most recent capacity addition. FERC's Phase VI docket (CP19-475-000; Federal Register 2019-06-21 and PHMSA special-permit notice 2019-07-29) independently corroborates a +78,000 dekatherms/day (~75-78 MMcf/d) firm-capacity addition that went in-service July 2022 (per gulfstreamgas.com/phase-vi/, 'completed and went in-service in July of 2022') — arithmetically consistent with capacity rising from ~1300 pre-Phase-VI to 1378 post-Phase-VI. Since Phase VI's in-service date (July 2022) predates the sheet's own LastUpdated stamp (2022-10-11), the 1310 MMcf/d figure appears to be stale relative to when it was recorded, not just outdated now. This is a genuine value disagreement, not a rounding difference (1310 vs 1378 = 5.2% off) — flagging as a spec concern for Update rather than overwriting; two independent origins (operator's current Fast Facts page + FERC/PHMSA regulator dockets) support 1378 MMcf/d as the current correct value.

This is a real, correctly-classified interstate-equivalent OCS gas trunk line (Fuel=Gas correct; not a gathering/process line — it exists specifically to move already-processed sales gas from the Independence Hub central processing platform to a downstream pipeline interconnect, the textbook definition of a transmission/export trunk), and it does not duplicate any other PID in the 50-row roster (no other Independence-, West Delta-, or Mississippi Canyon-named row exists in the roster; P0217 'Mississippi Canyon Gas Pipeline' is a physically distinct, separately-FERC/BOEM-tracked system per its own 44.5-mile length and different block numbers). Diameter=24in confirmed at high tier — every one of the seven documents opened (niobium.tech, OGJ x3, Anadarko PR, offshore-technology.com, Enterprise history) states 24 inches, no disagreement. Capacity=1000.00 MMcf/d confirmed at high tier and independently: niobium.tech states 'the requirements of 1.0 Billion Cubic Feet (BCF) per day gas throughput'; the Anadarko/BusinessWire release states 'the capacity to transport up to 1 Bcf/d'; OGJ's Nov-2006 special report states 'a capacity of 1 bcfd' — Enterprise (pipeline owner) and Anadarko (Hub operator, a different company) are two independent origins agreeing exactly, with OGJ trade press as a third. Fuel=Gas is trivially correct (every source describes a natural-gas trunk line). Status=operating confirmed: first gas flowed July 19, 2007 (Anadarko/BusinessWire release, dateline Jul 20 2007), and although OGJ reported the line was shut in after 'a leak that occurred Apr. 8' 2008 near a flex-joint in ~85 ft of water, repairs were completed and reduced-then-full volumes resumed by early-to-mid June 2008 (OGJ, 'Independence Trail pipeline resumes operations') — a repaired outage, not a status change, consistent with the BOEM-status rule for GoM lines (decommissioned/abandoned is a status finding; a repaired leak on an otherwise-live line is not). Owner1= Enterprise Products Partners 100% confirmed at high tier: Anadarko/BusinessWire ('100 percent owned and operated by Enterprise'), OGJ special report ('a wholly owned affiliate of Enterprise Products Partners LP'), and Enterprise's own company-history page all agree — two of these are origins independent of Enterprise itself (Anadarko, OGJ). Note in passing (not a tracker data issue): gem.wiki's own page is still tagged with the MediaWiki category 'Proposed pipelines in the United States' despite the article text and the sheet's Status=operating both being correct — a stale wiki-side category, not something that affects this row's GEM database values. Opened to exhaustion: niobium.tech PDF (full text), all three OGJ articles (full paragraph-level extraction), the archived Anadarko/BusinessWire release (full text), the archived offshore-technology.com project page, Enterprise's own history page, and Allseas' history page — 7 of the row's independently-found documents read in full, plus the sheet's own 3 harvested wiki citations (1 banned, 1 blocked/unverifiable, 1 used as the row's anchor primary source).

resolutions.recommendation: verify whether StartLocation/EndLocation should be swapped (Mississippi Canyon Block 920 as Start, West Delta Block 68 as End) to match actual gas-flow direction and this roster's own Start=upstream-field/End=downstream-delivery convention; separately, correct FuelSource off 'West Delta Block 68' to the actual upstream source (Independence Hub / Mississippi Canyon Block 920 fields)
resolutions.researcher_notes: Four independent sources describing the pipeline's function all agree on ONE gas-flow direction: Mississippi Canyon Block 920 (the Independence Hub central processing platform, the upstream source) toward West Delta Block 68 (a shallow-water manifold platform where the gas interconnects with — and is delivered into — Tennessee Gas Pipeline for onward transport to onshore markets). Anadarko/BusinessWire: 'connects the Hub platform to onshore markets via an interconnect with the Tennessee Gas Pipeline at Enterprise's West Delta block 68 shallow-water manifold platform.' OGJ (Jan 2006): pipeline 'will transport the gas to the Tennessee Gas Pipeline system in West Delta Block 68.' OGJ (Nov 2006 special report): 'connects the Independence Hub [platform] to an interconnect with Tennessee Gas Pipeline in West Delta Block 68.' Allseas (contractor, own history page): 'the pipeline transports gas from the Independence Hub Facility in Mississippi Canyon 920 to the West Delta 68 platform.' The sheet's current Location [ref] unit has StartLocation='West Delta Block 68' and EndLocation='Mississippi Canyon Block 920' — i.e. the REVERSE of the direction every independent source describes. The one source that reads consistently with the sheet's current direction is the sheet's own cited primary lead, niobium.tech (Jahde et al. 2007, written by the pipeline's own design engineers): 'ITP initiates from West Delta Block 68... and terminates at Mississippi Canyon Block 920' — but read in context this sentence is in the 'Pipeline Route Selection' section describing how the pipe-LAY vessel worked (shallow water to deep water), not the direction gas flows once in service; Allseas' own account of the SAME lay operation (Solitaire delivering the project in 2006) states the finished pipeline moves gas the opposite way. This roster's other offshore-to-onshore rows (P0223 Nautilus: 'Ship Shoal Block 207, Green Canyon Corridor -> Louisiana'; P0217 Mississippi Canyon Gas Pipeline: 'Mississippi Canyon -> Louisiana') consistently put the upstream field as Start and the downstream delivery point as End, so a swap here would also align this row with the roster's own convention. This is not a phantom-pipeline or duplicate concern — the place names in the Location cell are both correct and independently verified, it is only the Start/End assignment (and the copy of that assignment into FuelSource) that is doubtful. FuelSource is separately wrong on the same logic: the GEM schema gotcha for gas-sheet FuelSource is 'the upstream gas source feeding the line — a field, plant, or facility,' not a downstream delivery point, so 'West Delta Block 68' (the TGP interconnect/exit point) is very likely backwards for this column too; the correct value is the Independence Hub platform / the Atwater Valley-DeSoto Canyon-Lloyd Ridge-Mississippi Canyon field complex it gathers (OGJ special report names the ten anchor fields feeding the Hub). Left as a validity flag rather than an auto-fix per the 'never auto-apply a reference value' rule and because the StartState/Province='Gulf of Mexico' / EndState/Province='Gulf of Mexico' pair is genuinely defensible as written — this pipeline is subsea/offshore end-to-end between two OCS platforms and never itself makes onshore landfall in any state (delivery to shore happens downstream, inside Tennessee Gas Pipeline), so no state-name correction is proposed for either State/Province cell; this differs from the scope note's other flagged rows (Garden Banks, etc.) where a real state IS available.

resolutions.recommendation: flag LengthKnown=138.00 mi for review — the best-corroborated independent figure is 134 mi, not 138
resolutions.researcher_notes: Three distinct length figures circulate for this one pipeline, not two: (1) 140 miles / 225 km — Enterprise Products' own official company-history page ('a 24-inch, 140-mile pipeline at an estimated cost of $280 million') and offshore-technology.com's project page ('140 miles (225km) of 24in-diameter pipeline... total cost of the pipeline was estimated at $280m') both give this figure, and both attach it to the same $280m cost estimate — this is the ORIGINAL, pre-construction 2004 planning estimate, not an as-built number (Enterprise's history page places this sentence under the original 2004 Atwater Valley Producers Group agreement, before construction). (2) 134 miles — Oil & Gas Journal, in three separate articles, and the joint Anadarko/Enterprise/Devon/Eni/Hydro BusinessWire release on first production, state 'a new 134-mile, 24-in. pipeline' / 'the pipeline is approximately 134 miles long' / '134 miles on the seafloor' — OGJ's Nov-27-2006 special report gives this figure with the pipeline already S-laid (Allseas Solitaire completed the lay in August 2006), i.e. this is a near-as-built figure from two independent origins (OGJ the trade press, and Anadarko the Hub operator — a company distinct from Enterprise). (3) 138 miles — the sheet's current value, matching only the niobium.tech Jahde et al. 2007 conference paper written by the pipeline's own Enterprise design engineers, published after the line entered service. None of the three post-construction/as-built sources (OGJ x2 distinct events, Anadarko) agree with the sheet's 138; the only match is the single Enterprise engineering paper, which is a credible, specific, technical source but is one origin. Weight of independent evidence favors 134 mi over 138, but given a real engineering paper states 138 explicitly (not a rounding artifact — it is used consistently throughout that paper's methodology, e.g. in the deepwater length used for the world-record claim), this is presented as a flagged discrepancy for Baird to weigh rather than a value I'm confident enough to recommend silently overwriting. No fix applied; LengthKnown is left as-is on the sheet pending review.

resolutions.recommendation: verify Capacity/CapacityUnits against the original FERC certificate (docket CP15-17) -- likely a units conflation between MMcf/d and Dth/d, not just rounding

EIA's July 10, 2017 'Today in Energy' article (US government, independent of the operator) states explicitly: 'Sabal Trail Phase I is designed to have a total capacity of 810 million cubic feet per day (MMcf/d)' -- a different figure, in the SAME unit GEM uses (MMcf/d), not just a unit-conversion artifact. Separately, offshore-technology.com (a trade publication) states the Phase I capacity as 'approximately 830,000 dekatherms a day (Dth/day)' -- note Dth, not MMcf. Natural gas typically runs ~1.02-1.03 MMBtu(Dth) per Mcf, so 810 MMcf/d x ~1.025 =~ 830,000 Dth/d -- i.e. the 810-MMcf/d and 830,000-Dth/d figures plausibly describe the SAME underlying capacity in two different units (volumetric vs. energy-content), not a genuine disagreement on the physical capacity. That makes GEM's cell -- '830.00' explicitly labeled 'MMcf/d' -- look like it may have inherited the 830 figure from a Dth/d source without the unit conversion, which would overstate the true MMcf/d capacity by ~2.5%. The original 2014 FERC Notice of Intent (Federal Register, an independent regulatory source) gives yet a third, earlier planning-stage figure: 'an initial capacity of 800,000 dekatherms per day (Dth/d)'. None of the three sources found state '830 MMcf/d' outright. Flagging as a spec concern rather than silently passing -- recommend the researcher pull the actual FERC certificate order (CP15-17) or Sabal Trail's tariff for the authoritative Phase I design capacity and confirm the correct unit label.

This row is the first of three certificated construction phases of Transco's Hillabee Expansion Project (FERC Docket CP15-16), an interstate transmission loop expansion in Alabama built to deliver gas from Transco's Station 85 pooling point in Choctaw County to a new interconnect with Sabal Trail Transmission in Tallapoosa County. Independent confirmation across four distinct origins: (1) Pipeline & Gas Journal 'First Phase of Hillabee Expansion Completed' (Jul 2017) -- 818,410 Dth/d capacity add, ~20 miles of looping, Choctaw County compressor, in-service 2017; (2) Oil & Gas Journal 'Construction nears for Hillabee expansion project' -- Choctaw County to Tallapoosa County route, May 2017 target in-service, construction starting ~2016; (3) NS Energy Business project page (nsenergybusiness.com/projects/hillabee-expansion-project) -- segment-level loop breakdown (Proctor Creek 8.52km, Hissop 4.18km, Alexander City 12km, Billingsley 7.56km = 32.26km total new pipe), diameters (42in x3, 48in x1), counties (Choctaw, Coosa, Tallapoosa, Autauga, Chilton); (4) Transcontinental Gas Pipe Line Co LLC's own SEC Form 10-Q for Q2 2017 (sec.gov, filed by the regulated entity, not a press release) -- 'Hillabee Phase I increased capacity by 818 Mdth/d,' remainder placed in service July 11, 2017 (an earlier portion June 14, 2017). None of these are GEM-derived, none are abarrelfull/theodora, none cite each other. Status=operating, Fuel=Gas, PipelineType=transmission all confirmed by context (an in-service interstate gas transmission loop). StartYear1=2017 confirmed exactly (in-service June/July 2017). Capacity=818.00 MMcf/d confirmed near-exactly by two independent numeric restatements (PGJ: 818,410 Dth/d; SEC 10-Q: 818 Mdth/d) -- Dth and Mcf are functionally equivalent units for pipeline gas capacity, so this is a strong match, not just a plausible one. The existing sheet ref (eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php, a navigation page) is live but never names this specific phase and doesn't state 818 verbatim -- it should be supplemented (not deleted; it's live) with the sources below. DUPLICATE CHECK: NOT a duplicate of another roster row. Roster row P2544 (Transcontinental Gas Pipeline, Alabama, len=17.7, dia=42, cap=206.00) is very likely Hillabee Expansion Project PHASE 2 (the archived Business Wire Williams release on Phase II states capacity add of 206,660 Dth/d and ~11 miles of new pipe -- matches P2544's cap almost exactly) -- see cross_row_leads. P2733 (Phase 1) and P2544 (Phase 2) are legitimately distinct construction phases of the same certificated project with different mileage/diameter/in-service dates; keeping them as separate GEM rows is correct segment/phase-level granularity, not a double-count.

resolutions.researcher_notes: Reading FGT's original 2008 Phase VIII Notice of Intent (Federal Register E8-11695) to exhaustion turned up a scope wrinkle worth flagging even though it does not look like an actual duplicate. As ORIGINALLY proposed in 2008, Phase VIII was much bigger -- about 567.6 miles across 11 pipeline loops PLUS three greenfield lateral segments named 'Turkey Point Lateral' (6.7 mi, 24-in, Dade County FL), 'Manatee Lateral' (16.5 mi, 24-in, Manatee County FL), 'Suwannee Lateral' (22.0 mi, 20-in) and an 'Arcadia to FPL Martin Plant Lateral' (90.6 mi, 30-in) -- plus an outright acquisition of FPL's existing 20-in Martin Plant lateral. The task's roster of this batch's 17 FGT rows names exactly these segments among the OTHER 16 rows (Turkey Point Lateral / Alabama Power Lateral / Mobile Bay Lateral / etc.), so they clearly exist as separate GEM PIDs. But the AS-BUILT, in-service Phase VIII project that P4029 actually represents is only 483.2 miles (per the operator's own project page and EIA, both independent of the 2008 NOI) -- about 84 fewer miles than the 2008 proposal -- so at least some of those originally-proposed loops/laterals were evidently dropped, re-scoped, or deferred out of Phase VIII before it was finally certificated/built. I could NOT match any of them to a specific PID from the length/diameter columns in the 37-row roster given to me (none lines up cleanly with the 2008 proposal's preliminary specs, which is expected if the final built segment differs from the initial filing) -- so I am not asserting a specific duplicate PID, only flagging the scope history so whoever holds those sibling rows' shards can check their FERC docket numbers/build dates against CP09-17 and confirm they are NOT the same physical pipe P4029 already counts. This is a genuine finding from reading the source to exhaustion (rule 5), not a hunch. [QC] independent=yes claimed on 1 surviving ref(s) from 1 publisher(s) -> no.

resolutions.researcher_notes: The sheet's Owner1='Florida Gas Transmission Co LLC' at 100% is backwards. Citrus Corp. and Subsidiaries' own SEC-filed audited financial statements (filed as Exhibit 99.2 to an Energy Transfer Partners 8-K, FY2011) state verbatim: 'Citrus Corp. (Citrus), a holding company formed in 1986, owns 100 percent of the membership interest in Florida Gas Transmission Company, LLC (Florida Gas)... At December 31, 2011, the stock of Citrus was owned 50 percent by El Paso Citrus Holdings, Inc.,... and 50 percent by CrossCountry Citrus, LLC,... an indirect subsidiary of Southern Union Company.' In other words: Citrus Corp owns FGT LLC, not the other way around, and Citrus itself is a 50/50 joint venture. GEM's Owner field has 11 owner/percentage slots, which only makes sense if it is meant to capture the real equity chain -- as currently entered, the row states the pipeline owns itself, which is not informative and is technically incorrect. Two clearly independent origins: an SEC-filed, audited financial statement (Citrus Corp's own 10-K-style financials) vs. a PHMSA regulatory filing.

Independently confirmed via FERC's own Federal Register docket CP10-459-000 for the 'ETC Tiger Pipeline Expansion Project-Phase I' -- Notice of Application (75 FR 38799, published 2010-07-06) states ETC Tiger Pipeline, LLC (a subsidiary of Energy Transfer Partners, L.P.) filed on June 15, 2010 under NGA sec. 7(c) 'requesting: (1) Authorization to construct, own, operate and maintain approximately 20.5 miles of 42-inch diameter natural gas pipeline and 30,565 horsepower of compression located in Louisiana capable of transporting up to 400,000 Mcf/day (Expansion Project)'. The companion Notice of Intent to prepare an EA (75 FR 51033, published 2010-08-18) itemizes the construction: 'Loop 1 -- approximately 8.2 miles of new 42-inch diameter loop in Bienville Parish, Louisiana; and Loop 2 -- approximately 12.3 miles of new 42-inch diameter pipeline in Jackson and Ouachita Parishes, LA' plus added compression at Cannisnia (Red River Parish), Bienville, and Chatham (Jackson Parish) compressor stations, and states 'The Project would add 0.4 billion cubic feet/day of natural gas capacity to Tiger's system.' 8.2+12.3=20.5 mi -- GEM's LengthKnown=21.00 mi is within normal rounding. A second, fully independent origin (the industry project database offshore-technology.com, formerly hydrocarbons-technology.com -- same underlying page, redirected) corroborates from outside the FERC docket: 'The estimated cost of the expansion was $193m' (matches GEM SegmentCost=193,000,000 USD exactly), 'the extended pipeline has a capacity of 400,000mcf per day' (matches GEM Capacity=400.00 MMcf/d exactly, and independently confirms the FERC application's own figure), diameter 42 inches (matches), and 'The expansion project was submitted for approval to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission in June 2010 and was given certificate order in February 2011' (matches the FERC docket's June 2010 filing date; explains GEM's ConstructionYear=2011/StartYear1=2011 -- construction followed the Feb-2011 certificate, and the page separately notes the full system reached 2.4 Bcf/d, up from the original 2.0 Bcf/d, by August 2011, i.e. after this expansion entered service). No exact construction/in-service MONTH is stated anywhere I could reach this session, so Construction/Start stay at year-only confidence (medium-high) rather than high. CLASSIFICATION: correctly 'transmission' -- an FERC-jurisdictional NGA sec. 7(c) interstate certificate project, not a gathering/process line. DUPLICATE: checked against all 36 other rows in the 37-pipeline roster -- no match. Note for the record (not a duplicate flag, since no roster PID exists to name): the parent ~175-195-mile Carthage TX-to-Louisiana Tiger mainline (FERC Docket CP09-460, per Natural Gas Intelligence's 2010-02-02 environmental-nod article, and Energy Transfer Partners' 2009-02-20 open-season release, both read in full) is NOT itself a row in this 50-pipeline batch/roster -- it may be tracked under a different PID outside this Gulf Coast slice (e.g. the Texas batch, since its Texas terminus at Panola County/Carthage Hub would route there) or may not be tracked as its own GEM entity at all. Flagging for the orchestrator's awareness only; not enough information from this roster to call it Discovery or duplicate. ATTRIBUTION: StartState/Province is blank on the sheet (EndState/Province already reads 'Louisiana'). The FERC docket places the ENTIRE expansion (both loops + all three compressor-station upgrades) in Bienville, Jackson, Ouachita, and Red River Parishes -- all Louisiana, no Texas leg -- so StartState/Province should also read 'Louisiana', not stay blank (fill below). SPEC: Length, Diameter, Capacity, Construction/Start-year all confirmed as above. SegmentCost=193,000,000 USD is corroborated in only ONE place I could verify (offshore-technology.com) -- the FERC Notice of Application and the EA-scoping notice (both read to exhaustion) do not state a cost estimate; the actual FERC certificate order (which likely would) sits behind elibrary.ferc.gov's JS-rendered search, not reachable via curl this session, and both DuckDuckGo (returned HTTP 202, bot-challenge) and Bing (returned no scrapeable result body) failed to surface a second source, and the WebSearch tool had already exhausted its session-wide budget (200/200) by the time I reached this cell. SegmentCost therefore stays supported at medium tier pending that second origin -- flagging rather than force-closing it. CITATION-POOL ACCOUNTING: the wiki page harvested 6 citations. Opened/read: naturalgasintel.com (live, OK, read in full -- supports the PARENT CP09-460 mainline project, Haynesville Shale fuel sourcing, and the seven interstate interconnects, not the expansion's own numbers) and hydrocarbons-technology.com (redirects 301 to offshore-technology.com, live, OK, read in full -- the one source for SegmentCost). NOT usable: bit.ly/2sYGqrY resolves to A Barrel Full (abarrelfull.wikidot.com) -- banned source, never opened for citation purposes (standing rule 5). eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php is the generic navigation page the scope guidance already flags as non-citable for any specific value. casetext.com/federal-register/... returns HTTP 410 (confirmed dead, not merely blocked) and has no Wayback capture (`archive.org/wayback/available` returned an empty snapshot list) -- correctly retired, nothing to swap in. ir.energytransfer.com's 2009 open-season press release timed out live this session (ReadTimeout, an access failure, not a 404) -- per the never-delete-over-an-access-failure rule its Wayback snapshot (2017-05-06 capture) was added alongside and read in full instead; it corroborates the mainline's Carthage-to-near-Delhi route, Chesapeake Energy's 1.0 Bcf/d anchor shipper commitment, and the Haynesville Shale fuel source, but (being 2009, pre-expansion) says nothing about the Louisiana Expansion itself. Beyond the harvested pool, I independently found and read (via the Federal Register's own API, not this row's wiki citations) the two docket documents that are the strongest support for this specific expansion segment: FR 2010-16282 (Notice of Application) and FR 2010-20451 (Notice of Intent/EA scoping), both docket CP10-459-000.

resolutions.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, actively FERC-regulated interstate gas company, independent of GEM and independent of its own website. Kinetica Energy Express, LLC (KEE) holds NGA blanket certificate Docket No. CP12-489-000, originally granted when KEE was formed in 2012 specifically to acquire Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company's ('Tennessee'/Kinder Morgan) offshore-Gulf-of-Mexico + onshore-Louisiana 'Production Area Facilities' (Federal Register 2012-08-14, Docket CP12-489-000/CP12-490-000: 'Tennessee proposes to sell to Kinetica certain pipeline systems consisting of approximately 1,300 miles of various diameter pipeline, compression facilities at three locations totaling approximately 34,250 horsepower, twelve offshore platforms, and various appurtenant and auxiliary facilities'). KEE continues filing under that same blanket certificate through at least May 2026 (Federal Register 2026-05-13: KEE requests authorization for an 11,110-hp compressor addition in Pecan Island/Acadia Parish, Louisiana, 'to alleviate system deliverability constraints...on the mainline') -- 15 distinct Federal Register notices span 2012-2026, none GEM-derived. Kinetica Partners LLC's own PHMSA-related public-safety brochure (pipelinesafetyinfo.com, one of the 3 wiki-harvested citations) independently corroborates: 'Companies operating under the Kinetica umbrella are: Transmission -- Kinetica Energy Express, LLC, Kinetica Deepwater Express, LLC; Gathering -- Kinetica Midstream Energy, LLC,' explicitly placing KEE in the Transmission category (matching GEM's PipelineType=transmission) and stating the combined Kinetica system 'span[s] the Louisiana Gulf Coast from Cameron Parish to Plaquemines Parish' -- matching GEM's own Start=Plaquemines/End=Cameron almost exactly. offshore-technology.com (GlobalData market-data page, also wiki-harvested) is a 3rd independent source confirming a 1,139km/36in gas pipeline 'operated by Kinetica Partners.' CLASSIFICATION: transmission is correct (KEE is the umbrella's transmission arm, distinct from sister entity Kinetica Midstream Energy LLC, which holds the gathering lines -- not a classification error). DUPLICATE CHECK: compared against all 49 other rows in the 50-row Gulf Coast roster; no other row names Kinetica, and none of the other Louisiana intrastate/offshore lines (Acadian, Bridgeline, LIG, RIGS, Tiger, Nautilus, Garden Banks, Mississippi Canyon, Sea Robin, Chandeleur, Destin, Independence Trail) describe the Cameron-to-Plaquemines corridor -- no duplicate found. Note for a future sweep leg (not this roster): Kinetica also operates a distinct sister transmission company, 'Kinetica Deepwater Express, LLC,' per the same PSI brochure -- if GEM tracks that entity elsewhere under a different PID, it is NOT the same physical pipe as P6005 and should not be merged. WIKI CITATION POOL: all 3 harvested citations opened and read to exhaustion (offshore-technology.com, the PSI PDF, and the 2020-05-11 Federal Register abandonment notice); none were unreadable.

resolutions.recommendation: do not silently accept offshore-technology.com's 'starts at Texas' framing -- it conflicts with 2 independent sources and with GEM's own (correct) Location values; treat that one line on the GlobalData profile as unreliable
resolutions.researcher_notes: offshore-technology.com's prose states (twice, in both the visible text and its embedded schema block) that the pipeline 'starts at Texas (the US) and ends in Louisiana (the US).' This conflicts with GEM's current StartState/Province=Louisiana (StartLocation=Plaquemines) and with 2 independent sources: (1) Kinetica Partners' own PHMSA-adjacent safety brochure, which places the entire system 'from Cameron Parish to Plaquemines Parish' -- both in Louisiana, no Texas segment; (2) every Federal Register notice I read (2012, 2020, 2021, 2026) locates KEE's physical facilities exclusively in Louisiana parishes (Vermillion, Lafourche, Acadia) and the adjoining Gulf of Mexico OCS -- 'Texas' appears in these filings only as KEE's Houston, TX mailing/headquarters address, never as a pipeline terminus. My read: the GlobalData page's 'starts at Texas' line is most likely a template artifact that conflated the company's Houston HQ address (which the same GlobalData page separately and correctly states: 'Kinetica is headquartered in Houston, Texas') with the pipeline's physical start point. GEM's own StartState/Province=Louisiana is therefore CORRECT and independently corroborated -- no change recommended -- but this GlobalData source should not be cited for the Location cell precisely because of this internal contradiction (I did not propose it as a Location ref below). [QC] independent=yes claimed on 0 surviving ref(s) from 0 publisher(s) -> no; tier high -> medium (single source).

resolutions.researcher_notes: StartYear1=1960 is supported ONLY by the single offshore-technology.com/GlobalData line ('The Kinetica Energy Express project started operations in 1960'), which I could not corroborate with any second, independent source this session. Notably, Kinetica Energy Express, LLC did not exist as a certificated jurisdictional entity until 2012-2013 (FERC Docket CP12-489-000) -- '1960' is only plausible as the vintage of the underlying physical pipe when it was still part of Tennessee Gas Pipeline Company's system (TGP is one of the oldest US interstate systems and its Gulf Coast production-area facilities plausibly do predate 1960s-era construction), not as a date associated with the current corporate name. I searched for an independent second source (PHMSA NPMS/annual-report vintage data, a TGP-era FERC certificate order for the specific 'Production Area Facilities,' and Kinetica's own 'about'/history pages) but found nothing that states an in-service year for this system; kineticallc.com's about page returned 200 but contained no historical/founding-date prose I could extract. Staged at low tier rather than withheld, since GlobalData is a legitimate industry database and no source contradicts 1960 -- but this is a single-source value, flagged for further verification rather than treated as settled.
